title: The Canopy That Grew Itself Back Together

features.name: the join-point
features.desc-on-touch: Where two half-trunks learned their edges had been shaped to fit. The bark still shows the scar, but warmth moves through it now.

features.name: separation-traces
features.desc-on-touch: Wireframe geometry marking where the halves drifted. The render keeps the memory of the split even though the wood forgot it.

features.name: new-growth spiral
features.desc-on-touch: Fresh leaves in a corkscrew pattern where the wood learned to grow in both directions at once. The spiral was unexpected; the tree surprised itself.

features.name: the canopy's answer
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of filtered light where both sides of the crown meet. You can hear both birds singing from within it—they are the same song.

features.name: crown reaching
features.desc-on-touch: Branches that were learning to separate have grown back into a shared architecture. They reach together now, touching the sky as one shape.

features.name: the ground where they meet
features.desc-on-touch: The earth at the base has settled. Two root-systems learned to braid. The ground is richer here—more things grow.

inscription: two half-skies remember they are one sky

file.name: BirdCall_Duet_Reconciled_Canopy_1996.mp3

reverie.title: REVERIE — in the canopy at the hour it learned it was whole
narr: The sun hits both sides at once—she's on one branch,
you on another. The split is wide enough to make you feel
separate, but the light treats you as a single crown. "Listen,"
she says. "There's one bird calling from both sides now." You hear
it—not an echo, but a conversation where there used to be an argument.
The canopy settles around you both. You are the thing it grew back to have

exits.label: back down toward the first reconciliation
where the tree learns it has two hearts beating as one
into the crown's deepening auroral glow
down where roots learned to braid themselves
